deep.reconstruction:
PART A (end of a number-theoretic construction from the previous page). Setting: a number field k, with quadratic residue symbols (a/p) for prime ideals p. Two numbers π, κ are sought that satisfy a list of quadratic-residue conditions (1). The previous page reduced (1) to conditions (4) and (5). It then replaced the auxiliary numbers σ, ρ by σ*, ρ* satisfying (6). Next it chose a prime ideal 𝔶 with (ξ/σ*𝔶)=+1 for every unit ξ and every 'singular' number ξ, meaning (ξ)=𝔞² for some ideal 𝔞. From this σ*𝔶 is primary and 𝔶=(π) with σ*π a primary number.

This page repeats the step for κ. Choose a prime ideal η such that:
(i) (ξ/ρ*η)=+1 for all units ξ and all ξ with (ξ)=𝔞²;
(ii) (π/η)=(β/η).
Such η exists by Hilbert's Dirichlet-type density theorem for prime ideals with prescribed quadratic characters (my gloss). Condition (i) puts ρ*η in the principal genus and makes it primary. 'As before' Hilbert then concludes η=(κ) is principal with ρ*κ primary. Condition (ii) is exactly the last equation of (5), (π/(κ))=(β/(κ)). By the previous page, the other equations of (5) follow from the reciprocity laws once π and κ are prime to 2. The conditions (4) are inherited from (6) through the primary numbers σ*π and ρ*κ. Hence π and κ satisfy all of (1). This is the standard auxiliary-prime technique of Hilbert's theory of relative quadratic fields (Math. Ann. 51, 1899).

PART B (foundations of geometry). In the 1899 Festschrift (Grundlagen der Geometrie) the axiom groups are I incidence, II order, III parallels, IV congruence, V continuity. There Hilbert showed that Pascal's (Pappus') theorem cannot be derived from Desargues' theorem using I, II, III; the model is a non-Archimedean, non-commutative ordered skew field. He now proposes the converse independence: Desargues should not be provable from Pascal in the plane using only I 1-2 (plane incidence), II and III.

Planned method:
- Postulate a weak angle-congruence structure: unique transfer of angles; the theorems on equality of opposite/alternate (and vertical/adjacent) angles; and an angle-subtraction rule.
- The subtraction rule: rays OA, OB, OC, OD lie in that order (figure). If ∠AOC=∠BOD then ∠AOB=∠DOC. Writing ∠AOB=x, ∠BOC=y, ∠COD=z gives x+y=y+z, so x=z.
- With these statements, Sommer's proof (reproduced in the Festschrift) proves Pascal, since equality of inscribed angles on the same chord follows from them (next page).
- Implicit aim (mine): construct a plane where these angle facts, hence Pascal, hold but Desargues fails, proving independence.

On the next page Hilbert already doubts this: with the Archimedean axiom, and 'perhaps even so', Desargues probably follows ('wahrscheinlich').
errors: Part A: the passage from 'ρ*η is primary / has all characters +1 on units and singular numbers' to 'η is principal, η=(κ)' is not valid for a general class group. Character conditions on singular numbers only fix the genus, i.e. the class modulo squares. Hilbert himself flags this on the previous page: for classes of order 4, biquadratic characters are needed, 'etc.'. The step is fully justified only when the class group is suitably restricted (e.g. elementary 2-group); otherwise the conditions must be strengthened.

Part B: the programme cannot succeed as stated. Hessenberg (1905) proved that Pappus/Pascal implies Desargues from the plane incidence axioms alone; the degenerate-case gaps were later closed. A fortiori this holds with order and parallel axioms. So the hoped-for independence ('Desargues nicht mit Hilfe des Pascalschen ... bewiesen werden kann') is false. Hilbert's own note on the next page ('vielleicht doch der Desargues? wahrscheinlich') anticipates this.
Part B: the angle-subtraction rule ∠AOC=∠BOD ⇒ ∠AOB=∠DOC presupposes the ray order A,B,C,D, as in the figure. Without that order it is false in general.

results.what: Existence of auxiliary prime ideals η with prescribed quadratic characters (on units, singular numbers and given numbers π, β), chosen principal with ρ*κ primary, to satisfy a system of residue conditions
results.modern_name: Auxiliary-prime / Dirichlet density argument in genus theory of relative quadratic extensions (precursor of Hasse norm theorem arguments)
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert, Über die Theorie des relativquadratischen Zahlkörpers (1899)

results.what: Recalled: Pascal's theorem not derivable from Desargues with axioms I–III (without Archimedes)
results.modern_name: Independence of Pappus from Desargues (non-commutative ordered skew field model)

results.what: Proposed converse: Desargues not provable from Pascal using I1-2, II, III, via a weak angle-congruence model in which Sommer's proof of Pascal works
results.modern_name: Converse of Hessenberg's theorem (Pappus ⇒ Desargues); the conjectured independence is false
results.usually_credited_to: Question settled by G. Hessenberg (1905), Pappus implies Desargues

results.what: Angle subtraction: ∠AOC=∠BOD ⇒ ∠AOB=∠DOC for rays in order A,B,C,D

deep.surprise_reason: The number theory is routine Hilbert material. Of some historical interest: c.1899-1900, before Hessenberg 1905, Hilbert explicitly posed whether Desargues follows from Pascal in the plane. He first tried to prove independence, then on the next page suspected the implication holds. It is a notable unpublished detail but not a result.

transcription_corrections: 'Gegen- und Nebenwinkel': the manuscript most likely reads 'Gegen- und Wechselwinkel' (cf. next page 'Gegen- und Wechselwinkel bei Parallelen').
'mit Hilfe' is written 'mit Hülfe' in the manuscript.

'für alle ξ = Einheiten und = Zahlen, die = Quadrate von Idealen sind': the third '=' before 'Quadrate' is unclear in the image and may be 'ξ' or '≡'; the sense is 'numbers that are squares of ideals'.
Struck-through 'Man' before 'Zum Beweise' and struck 'den Satz, dass' are correctly marked; the struck word before 'Sommer'schen' reads 'dem' or 'des'.
